summary: THE FIT IS MEASURED ON BOTH SIDES WITH THE SAME INSTRUMENT AND IT IS 0.1000 mm PER SIDE, EXACTLY, ON BOTH AXES. cecad.meshfeatures.intervals ray-cast calipers on ankle_left.stl: blocks x 34.1000..39.1000 and 60.9000..65.9000 (5.0000 mm each, constant across y 31.8..35.5), ribs y 31.6630..33.1630 and 34.1630..35.6630 (1.5000 mm each, 1.0000 mm gap, envelope 4.0000 mm), heights z -21.3420..-15.2810 (6.0610) and -21.3420..-13.3420 (8.0000). Same instrument on foot_left.stl: pockets x 34.0000..39.2000 and 60.8000..66.0000 (5.2000 mm each), y 31.5630..35.7630 (4.2000 mm), closed at y 31.4 and 35.8, and OPEN top to bottom in z at all five stations probed. 5.2000-5.0000 = 0.2000 in x, 4.2000-4.0000 = 0.2000 in y. Pair pitch 26.8000 mm. The cradle that carries the load: the ankle's under-hull circle-fits to R16.3058 (residual mean 0.00432, 49 pts) at x 40 and R16.3018 (0.00396, 48 pts) at x 60, about a centre 0.007-0.011 mm from the declared ankle axis. compat.py graded the real pair live: interface_names, pair_pitch, clearance, cradle and claims_a_snap PASS.
by: claude (microduck lane T), cecad.meshfeatures + meshslice on Pollen's meshes

summary: THE SLUG SAYS SNAP AND NOTHING SNAPS — RECORDED, NOT SMOOTHED. Searched both meshes for an undercut, barb, lip or lead-in on either side of this joint. None exists: (1) the pockets are open top to bottom in z — cecad.meshfeatures.intervals along z at (36.5, 32.4), (36.5, 34.9), (63.5, 32.4), (34.2, 32.4) and (39.0, 32.4) returns NO material at all — so there is no lip for a barb to pass; (2) the blocks are prismatic over their whole height, x span constant 34.1000..39.1000 across y 31.8..35.5 and single unbroken z spans; (3) the fit is a 0.1000 mm per-side CLEARANCE, which cannot snap into anything. What retains the foot is the single M2 at (x 50.0000, y 4.5020): ankle `foot_screw` (Ø2.2 through a 2.5 mm plate with a Ø4.4 x 1.0 counterbore) into foot `ankle_screw` (Ø1.6 x 5.5 thread-forming pilot with a Ø3.0 x 0.5 relief on a Ø5 boss), connection:threaded-m2. The slug is kept because both parts' `accepts` lists already carry it and renaming would dangle; the CLAIM is corrected everywhere and compat.py's `claims_a_snap` FAILs any row that reasserts it while mate() refuses params['snap_force_N'] outright — both verified live 2026-09-02.

THE AS-PRINTED FIT IS NOT DECIDABLE FROM THE MODEL. 0.1000 mm per side is a QUARTER of a 0.4 mm FDM extrusion width; slicer compensation, elephant's foot and the corner radius a nozzle leaves each move a printed pocket by that much or more, so whether a real block slides into a real pocket or binds cannot be read off the mesh. What settles it: calipers on a printed block and its pocket, stated as measured_pocket_mm on the pocket interface. Also open: the load share between the two R16.3 end ledges and the R16.5 relief band that stands 0.2000 mm clear of the hull — a contact question, not a geometry one. Also recorded: lane T's own circle fits of the foot's ledges at x 33.5 and 66.5 were REJECTED rather than published (R16.556-16.646, residual mean 0.031-0.044 mm) because the annulus window catches the relief band with the ledge; the foot folder's own R16.3 / R16.5 figures stand.

THE FOLDER WORKS THROUGH THE ONE INTEGRATION SEAM, not just when run directly. cecad.triad.mate("connection:snap-fit-ankle-blocks", a_iface, b_iface, params) — TRIAD.md's single seam, the call every other app (ce-struct, ce-pcb, ce-wire, the APIs) reaches this folder through — was invoked live on the reference interface pair on 2026-09-02 and mate() returned dof_left [], adds [], holds_by 'form', with the tz caveat carried in joint.axes_cannot_determine (locked only once the M2 is driven, because the pockets are open top to bottom). Run in FreeCAD's python 3.11 with CE_TRIAD_ROOT set to this repo plus ce-workshop. All four connection folders authored in this lane were exercised the same way in the same run and all four returned; none raised.
by: claude (microduck lane T), cecad.triad.mate through the loader
